questions.statement: My father ___ coffee before he goes to work.
questions.context: Choose the form that matches a daily routine with a third person subject.

options.feedback: Correct! A daily routine with a third person singular subject takes the present simple with -s.
The present continuous describes an action happening now, not a repeated morning habit.
The base form lacks the -s that the third person singular requires.
The present perfect would link the drinking to the present moment, which a routine does not need.

questions.explanation:
The present simple covers habits and routines. The subject is third person singular, so the verb form must agree: drink becomes drinks.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Last week the students ___ a short report about the local river.
questions.context: Complete the past simple of a regular verb.

options.feedback: Correct! Write is irregular, and its past simple is wrote.
English does not add -ed to irregular verbs, and writed is not a form of write.
Written is the past participle, used after have or was, not the simple past on its own.
A past simple cannot be built on the auxiliary has, and wrote is already a past form.

questions.explanation:
Regular verbs take -ed in the past simple, but write is irregular. Its three forms are write, wrote, written, and only wrote serves as the simple past.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: They ___ on the project since March and there is still a lot to do.
questions.context: The action started in the past and is still not finished.

options.feedback: Correct! Since March with an activity still running takes the present perfect continuous.
A present continuous would lose the link with the starting time given by since March.
The bare present simple would treat the work as a general habit rather than a continuous effort since a date.
The past perfect continuous would need a past reference point, and since March is still part of the present period.

questions.explanation:
Since plus a month names the start of an open period. An activity that has not stopped within that period takes the present perfect continuous.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: While the children ___ their homework, the lights went out.
questions.context: One action was under way when another interrupted it.

options.feedback: Correct! The longer action already in progress takes the past continuous.
The past simple would make both actions short and separate, losing the sense of interruption.
A present continuous would place the homework in the present, which the scene in the past denies.
The past perfect would place the homework completely before the blackout, removing the overlap.

questions.explanation:
While introduces the background action and when usually introduces the interruption. The background is past continuous, the interruption is past simple.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: By the time the ambulance arrived, the driver ___ already called for help.
questions.context: The earlier event is complete before a past reference point.

options.feedback: Correct! The call happened before the ambulance arrived, so had plus participle is required.
The present perfect would connect the call to now, but the reference point is the arrival, which is in the past.
A past continuous would suggest the call was still in progress, and already signals a completed action.
A future form is impossible in a sequence of events the sentence presents as finished.

questions.explanation:
By the time is a past boundary, and already confirms the action finished before it. Together they point firmly at the past perfect.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: I am soaked. I ___ need a towel.
questions.context: A prediction made at the moment of speaking.

options.feedback: Correct! A prediction or statement made now is expressed with will.
Be going to points to an intention or to evidence from before this moment, and this is an instant assessment.
A present perfect would report a completed need, but the sentence is about a demand for the coming minutes.
A past continuous belongs to a past scene, and there is no past reference in the situation.

questions.explanation:
Will carries decisions, promises, refusals and predictions made at the moment of speaking. The soaked clothes are the immediate evidence behind the statement.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ___ you ever ___ to the archaeological site?
questions.context: Complete the question with the correct auxiliary.

options.feedback: Correct! Ever in an experience question takes the present perfect, and been is the participle of be.
Did with ever is not used, and the base form be cannot follow an auxiliary that already carries the tense.
Being is the -ing form and belongs to continuous tenses, not to the present perfect.
A present continuous would ask about the moment of speaking, not about life experience.

questions.explanation:
Experience questions use the present perfect, and the form of be in that structure is have been. The negative form is have never been.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: By 2018 the city ___ a completely new bus network.
questions.context: Choose the form required after 'by' plus a past year.

options.feedback: Correct! The network was in place before the deadline year, so the past perfect is correct.
The present perfect would mean the network was introduced at any time up to now, ignoring the 2018 deadline.
A bare base form after by would carry no tense marking at all.
The future perfect looks forward from a future point, and 2018 is already in the past.

questions.explanation:
By plus a past year looks back from that year. Anything completed before that point belongs to the past perfect, and anything later is irrelevant to the sentence.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: These shoes ___ no size eleven.
questions.context: A stative verb that has no continuous form.

options.feedback: Correct! Have used as possession or absence does not take the continuous in this meaning.
Stative verbs such as have, know and believe do not normally form a continuous here.
Has is the third person singular form, and the subject these shoes is plural.
The past simple would place the absence of size eleven in the past, and nothing in the sentence requires that.

questions.explanation:
Stative verbs describe a state rather than an action. Used for possession they take the simple form, and the plural subject here is followed by have.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: After the exam we ___ to visit the museum, and we already bought the tickets.
questions.context: A plan and an intention that already existed.

options.feedback: Correct! Tickets already bought prove the plan existed before this moment, so be going to is right.
Will would suggest the decision is being taken now, but the purchase shows it was taken earlier.
The present perfect would report a completed visit, and the tickets show the visit is still ahead.
A past continuous would place the intention in a past scene, but the exam is still ahead.

questions.explanation:
Evidence that a decision predates the moment of speaking selects be going to over will. Buying the tickets is that evidence.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: I ___ the door. It was open when I passed.
questions.context: The signal 'just' places the action in the present period.

options.feedback: Correct! Just is a present perfect marker and the door state shows the action has just happened.
A past simple with just is not used; just belongs to the present perfect in this function.
A present continuous would suggest the action is still under way, but the state of the door shows it finished.
The past perfect would need a past reference point later than the closing, and there is none.

questions.explanation:
Just, already, yet and never are present perfect markers. Together with the present result they make the present perfect the only coherent reading.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If it rains tomorrow, the match ___.
questions.context: A real condition with a probable future result.

options.feedback: Correct! The first conditional pairs a present condition with a likely future result.
'Would' belongs to the second conditional, which describes an unreal or doubtful situation.
A present simple after if could be a zero conditional about a rule, not a prediction about tomorrow.
The present perfect would place the cancellation in a completed period before now.

questions.explanation:
The first conditional is the open and likely case: if plus present, will plus base verb. Tomorrow makes the condition a real future possibility.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: If you heat ice, it ___.
questions.context: A general truth expressed in a conditional clause.

options.feedback: Correct! A zero conditional states a general truth with present simple in both clauses.
The future simple in both clauses would turn a general truth into a single future prediction.
'Would' describes an unreal condition, and heating ice certainly is not unreal.
The present perfect would place the melting in a completed period, which a general truth does not have.

questions.explanation:
The zero conditional expresses facts that are always true. Both clauses take the present simple, and no future or past tense appears anywhere in the structure.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: They ___ for six hours before the storm reached the coast.
questions.context: The action began in the past and continued up to a past deadline.

options.feedback: Correct! A duration that ended at a past reference point takes the past perfect continuous.
The present perfect continuous would measure the driving up to now, but the storm is in the past.
A past continuous would describe the drive as ongoing without fixing its duration as completed.
The future perfect would measure forward from a future point, and the storm has already passed.

questions.explanation:
The past perfect continuous measures a closed duration. Before the storm reached the coast supplies the past moment at which the six hours came to an end.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: He ___ never ___ sushi, but he loves fried food.
questions.context: A negative statement covering all time up to now.

options.feedback: Correct! Never with no past time point covers the whole life up to now, so the present perfect negative fits.
Did refers to a definite past occasion, and the sentence deliberately gives no time.
After have the verb must be a participle, and ate is the past simple form.
A past continuous would place the eating in a past scene, which the life-long scope excludes.

questions.explanation:
Never plus no time expression is a strong present perfect pattern. The participle form of eat is eaten, and it follows has without any further marking.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: By June last year the builders ___ the whole first floor ___; today they are working on the second.
questions.context: The reference point decides between two perfect tenses.

options.feedback: Correct! The first floor was complete by the past deadline, and but contrasts that with the work going on now.
The present perfect would place the finishing in the present period, ignoring the closed June deadline, and so gives a result rather than a contrast.
Because gives a reason, but today's work is a contrast to the completed floor, not the cause of it.
The future perfect would project from a future point, and June last year is already closed.

questions.explanation:
Two reference points appear in the sentence: the past deadline in the first clause and the present moment in the second. Each clause takes the tense that matches its own reference point.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: He ___ not come to the party last week; he was ill.
questions.context: The negative form of a modal in a past situation.

options.feedback: Correct! Could not expresses the past inability that explains his absence.
Must not expresses a prohibition or a deduction, not an inability to attend.
Would not is used for refusals and for unreal past situations, not for a simple past inability.
Should not expresses advice or an expectation that was not followed, which is a different claim.

questions.explanation:
Modal ability and permission have a past form: could and might. The reason given for the absence is illness, which is exactly what could not reports.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: While the guide ___ about the castle, a visitor asked a question.
questions.context: Two overlapping past actions, one much longer than the other.

options.feedback: Correct! The background speech is the past continuous and the question is the interruption.
The past simple would reduce the speech to one finished act with no overlap.
A present continuous would place the speech now, and the visit to the castle is already over.
The present perfect would connect the speech to now, which the past setting denies.

questions.explanation:
When two past actions overlap, the longer one takes the past continuous and the shorter one the past simple. While normally introduces the longer action.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The government ___ a new law in March and it came into force in June.
questions.context: A completed action with no reference to the present.

options.feedback: Correct! A finished past time such as in March requires the past simple.
The present perfect cannot stand with in March, because that time closes the action off from the present.
The present simple would place the passing now, which the month denies.
The past perfect would need a past point later than March, and the law came into force rather than being needed earlier.

questions.explanation:
A precise past date is a finished time and takes the past simple. The present perfect is reserved for actions whose present relevance is being reported.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: She ___ down the stairs and fell.
questions.context: The correct form of a frequently used irregular verb.

options.feedback: Correct! Run is irregular and its past simple is ran.
The -ed ending is for regular verbs, and runned is not a form of run.
The base form cannot serve as the past simple after a subject and before another past verb.
The past participle of run is run, and the auxiliary has requires the participle form.

questions.explanation: Irregular verbs must be learned in all three forms. Run, ran, run is one of the irregular patterns where the participle looks like the base form.
questions.subject: ingles
